summary.whatChanges: Negative q-values in Accept headers are now clamped to 0 instead of 1, so refused types sort last instead of first. Values above 1 and NaN still clamp to 1. Tests updated to assert the new ordering.
behaviorChanges: `q=-1` (or any negative q) now yields quality 0 instead of 1, placing that media type last in the sorted result
`q=-Infinity` still maps to 0, but now via the generic negative branch rather than a special case
Content negotiation no longer selects a type the client explicitly refused with a negative q over a legitimately weighted one
`q=Infinity` and other out-of-range positive values continue to clamp to 1; NaN still clamps to 1
risks: Callers that relied on negative q being treated as highest priority will see different negotiated responses
Clamping (rather than rejecting) makes the q sequence non-monotonic, so results depend on the sort being stable/correct for equal q values
Malformed headers containing negative q now silently produce a 0-quality entry rather than an error, which may mask client bugs
